questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the DIKW hierarchy.
I. Information consists of raw facts that have not been processed or given any context.
II. Information is data that has been processed and organised so that it has meaning.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: Raw, unprocessed facts are data. Processing and organising data gives it meaning and produces information, so I is false and II is true.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about types of knowledge.
I. Tacit knowledge can be easily codified and stored in manuals.
II. Explicit knowledge can be documented and shared through manuals and databases.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: Explicit knowledge is formal and can be written down. Tacit knowledge is personal, rooted in experience and hard to articulate, so it cannot easily be codified; I is false.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of explicit knowledge?
questions.e: Explicit knowledge is documented and codified, as in manuals, reports and databases.

questions.q: In the SECI model, the letters S, E, C and I stand for
questions.e: SECI means Socialisation, Externalisation, Combination and Internalisation.

questions.q: The SECI model of knowledge creation was proposed by
questions.e: Ikujiro Nonaka and Hirotaka Takeuchi presented the SECI model in The Knowledge-Creating Company (1995).

questions.q: The term "knowledge worker" was coined by
questions.e: Peter Drucker introduced the term in the 1950s-60s for people who work mainly with knowledge.

questions.q: Peter Senge popularised the concept of the learning organisation in his book
questions.e: The Fifth Discipline (1990) by Peter Senge describes the learning organisation.

questions.q: A group of people who share a concern or passion for something and learn to do it better by interacting regularly is a
questions.e: Communities of practice, a term from Lave and Wenger, are groups that learn together around a shared domain.

questions.q: A knowledge portal is best described as
o: a single web gateway to an organisation's knowledge resources
a hardware device for storing knowledge
questions.e: A knowledge portal gives users one access point to documents, experts and tools.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a component of intellectual capital?
questions.e: Intellectual capital consists of human, structural and relational (customer) capital. Land and buildings are physical assets.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the SECI model.
I. Socialisation is the conversion of explicit knowledge into tacit knowledge.
II. Combination is the conversion of tacit knowledge into explicit knowledge.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: Socialisation converts tacit knowledge to tacit knowledge through shared experience. Combination converts explicit knowledge to explicit knowledge by merging and organising documented knowledge. Both statements are false.

questions.q:
Regarding the SECI model, consider the following.
I. Externalisation converts tacit knowledge into explicit concepts.
II. Internalisation converts explicit knowledge into tacit knowledge.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are true. Externalisation articulates tacit knowledge as explicit concepts, and internalisation absorbs explicit knowledge into personal, tacit know-how.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT an objective of a knowledge audit?
o: Identifying the knowledge needs of the organisation
Locating existing knowledge resources and how knowledge flows
Finding gaps between the knowledge needed and available
Calculating the organisation's income tax liability
questions.e: A knowledge audit examines knowledge needs, resources, flows and gaps. Computing tax liability belongs to financial accounting and is unrelated.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the knowledge economy.
I. Knowledge and skills are the main source of competitive advantage.
II. Knowledge is used up when it is shared, as land and oil are.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: Knowledge is the key resource, and unlike physical resources it is not used up by sharing.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of Senge's five disciplines of a learning organisation?
questions.e: The five disciplines are personal mastery, mental models, shared vision, team learning and systems thinking.

questions.q: Which KM technology is used to discover previously unknown patterns in large collections of data?
questions.e: Data mining searches large data sets for hidden patterns and is a knowledge discovery tool.

questions.q: Match the SECI mode in List I with the conversion in List II.
questions.e: Socialisation is tacit to tacit, externalisation is tacit to explicit, combination is explicit to explicit and internalisation is explicit to tacit.

questions.q: In Nonaka's theory of knowledge creation, "ba" refers to
o: a shared context or space in which knowledge is created and shared
a coding scheme for explicit knowledge
questions.e: Ba is a shared physical, virtual or mental space that supports knowledge creation.

questions.q: The concept of tacit knowledge, summed up as "we can know more than we can tell", was introduced by
questions.e: Michael Polanyi introduced tacit knowing in The Tacit Dimension (1966). Nonaka later applied it to organisations.

questions.q: Leif Edvinsson is associated with pioneering the reporting of intellectual capital at which company?
questions.e: Edvinsson was the first corporate director of intellectual capital at the Swedish firm Skandia.
